title: Pope Leo Leaves Hospital, Days After Lung Cancer Surgery
text:

‘I Am Much Better, Thank You’: Pope Leo Leaves Hospital, Days After Lung Surgery
Leo XIV had been treated for lung cancer at Gemelli Hospital in Rome.
Pope Leo XIV was discharged from a Rome hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery to remove a tumor from his right lung.
The pope left Gemelli Hospital at about 3:30 p.m., arriving at the Vatican after a 10-minute car journey, roughly three days earlier than the Vatican had originally suggested for when he would return to his residence.
“I am much better, thank you,” he said in English to a journalist who asked about his health as he was driven from the hospital grounds.
Vatican officials said he would deliver his weekly prayer and blessing on Sunday from his apartment overlooking St. Peter’s Square, although all of his private audiences are suspended until Tuesday.
In a statement released on Saturday by the Vatican, Leo’s doctors said that he had undergone routine checkups and a chest X-ray had revealed that the affected lung was healing well. They said that he was “fit for discharge.”
Dozens of onlookers cheered as he walked out of the hospital, some of them shouting, “Long live the pope.” He paused briefly to greet patients, some of whom held intravenous poles; shook hands with medical staff; and thanked the surgeon who conducted his operation.
